checks.claim: Each escalator step has wheels running in two separate tracks that keep the step level.
checks.why: HowStuffWorks: front wheels on the step-wheel track, back wheels on the trailer-wheel track, spaced so each step stays level.

sources.title: How Escalators Work: Steppin' Out - HowStuffWorks

checks.claim: A motor at the top of an escalator turns gears that pull the step chain.
checks.why: An electric motor at the top turns the drive gears that move the pair of step chains.

checks.claim: Escalators have a brake that stops the steps if the power fails.
checks.why: California Title 8: the brake shall be applied automatically if the power supply is interrupted; brakes are spring-set and fail-safe.

sources.title: California Code of Regulations Title 8 section 3090

checks.claim: An escalator's handrail moves at about the same speed as the steps.
checks.why: Patents drive the handrail from the step drive at substantially the same speed; technicians set it slightly ahead, so 'about the same' holds.

sources.title: US4895240A - Cogbelt handrail drive for passenger conveyor
